title: Spaghetti Aglio e Olio
description: Spaghetti tossed with olive oil, gently toasted sliced garlic and red pepper flakes, with starchy pasta water pulling it into a glossy sauce.
scaleNote: A 12-inch skillet holds about 1 pound of spaghetti. For a bigger batch, cook the garlic and toss the pasta in a wide Dutch oven instead.

image.alt: Illustration of a plate of spaghetti with sliced garlic, parsley and chili flakes

ingredients.scaleNote: A big pot of water cooks any batch size, so it stays the same.

ingredients.prep: for the pasta water, plus more to taste
ingredients.scaleNote: Seasons the pot of water, which stays the same size at any batch.

ingredients.note: up to {qty 1 tsp} for more heat

steps.text: Bring the water to a boil in a large covered pot, then uncover it and stir in the salt.

Add the spaghetti and cook, stirring now and then, until it bends easily but is still firm in the center, {time 7-8 min}, or about {time 2 min notimer} short of the package time. It finishes cooking in the sauce.

While the pasta cooks, put the oil and garlic in a {len 12 in} skillet over medium-low heat. Cook, stirring often, until the garlic is pale gold and fragrant, {time 4-6 min}. It keeps darkening off the heat, so stop at pale gold rather than brown.
Take the skillet off the heat and stir in the red pepper flakes. Scoop out {qty 1 cup} of the pasta water, then drain the spaghetti and add it to the skillet with {qty 1/2 cup} of the reserved water.

Set the skillet over medium-high heat and toss constantly with tongs until the water and oil come together into a light, glossy sauce that clings to the pasta, {time 2-3 min}. Add more pasta water a splash at a time if it looks dry or oily.
Take the pan off the heat and toss in the parsley. Taste, add a pinch of salt if needed and serve right away, because the sauce tightens as it cools.

notes: Slice the garlic as thin and even as you can so it all turns golden at the same time. Thick slices stay pale while thin ones burn.
If you're not cooking vegan, a little grated Parmesan or pecorino over each plate is a good addition.
Best eaten right away. Leftovers keep in the fridge for up to 3 days; warm them in a skillet with a splash of water.
